```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

`pertsig` provides perturbation signatures: per-gene logistic regression
weights that describe the transcriptional response to a perturbation (a
drug, a cytokine, a gene knockout and so on). `getGeneSets()` turns each
signature into gene sets of its top-weighted genes, which can be tested
against a differential expression (DE) profile with
[fgsea](https://bioconductor.org/packages/fgsea/).

## Installation

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("alserglab/pertsig")
```

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(pertsig)
library(fgsea)
library(GEOquery)
library(limma)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Loading signatures

Signatures are available for human (`"hsa"`) and mouse (`"mmu"`). The file
is downloaded once and cached. Rows can be named by gene symbol or Entrez ID;
here we use gene symbols to match the microarray annotation below.

```{r}
signatures <- loadSignatures("hsa", geneId = "symbol")
dim(signatures)
head(colnames(signatures), 10)
```

Each column is one signature, that could include one or several perturbations 
(that were megered together because they couldn't be reliably distinguished). 
Weights are signed: positive weights mark genes that go up after the perturbation and
negative weights mark genes that go down. 
For gene-related signatures, the positive direction corresponds to up-regulated genes in 
the gene-activating perturbations (e.g., overexpression) and down-regulated in 
the gene-inhibiting perturbations (e.g., gene knockout).

```{r}
weights <- signatures[, "IFNG"]
topSets <- getGeneSets(signatures[, "IFNG", drop = FALSE], topK = 10, direction = "both")
topGenes <- data.frame(gene = unlist(topSets), weight = weights[unlist(topSets)])

ggplot(data.frame(weight = weights), aes(weight)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 100) +
    geom_point(data = topGenes, aes(x = weight, y = 1), colour = "firebrick") +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = topGenes, aes(x = weight, y = 1, label = gene),
                             size = 3, nudge_y = 1, direction = "both",
                             max.overlaps = Inf, min.segment.length = 0) +
    scale_y_continuous(transform = "log1p", breaks = c(0, 1, 10, 100, 1000)) +
    labs(title = "IFNG signature weights", x = "Weight", y = "Genes (log scale)")

```

## Example dataset

[GSE41291](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE41291) is a
microarray time course of the HSG cell line, untreated or treated with
IFN-alpha or IFN-gamma, in triplicate. We use the 4-hour samples and make two
DE comparisons: IFN-alpha vs untreated and IFN-gamma vs untreated.

```{r, message = FALSE}
gse <- getGEO("GSE41291", AnnotGPL = TRUE)[[1]]
gse$condition <- sub("^HSG (\\S+) .*$", "\\1", gse$title)
gse$time <- sub("^HSG \\S+ (\\S+) rep\\d+$", "\\1", gse$title)
gse4hr <- gse[, gse$time == "4hr"]

table(gse4hr$condition)
```

fgsea needs one statistic per gene, so before fitting we drop probes
without a unique gene symbol, keep the most highly expressed probe of each
gene, and keep the 12,000 most highly expressed genes:

```{r}
symbols <- fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol`
gse4hr <- gse4hr[!is.na(symbols) & symbols != "" & !grepl("///", symbols, fixed = TRUE), ]
gse4hr <- gse4hr[order(rowMeans(exprs(gse4hr)), decreasing = TRUE), ]
gse4hr <- gse4hr[!duplicated(fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol`), ]

gse4hr <- gse4hr[seq_len(min(12000, nrow(gse4hr))), ]
featureNames(gse4hr) <- fData(gse4hr)$`Gene symbol`
dim(gse4hr)
```


## Differential expression

```{r}
condition <- factor(gse4hr$condition, levels = c("untreated", "IFNalpha", "IFNgamma"))
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + condition)
colnames(design) <- levels(condition)

contrasts <- makeContrasts(IFNalpha = IFNalpha - untreated,
                           IFNgamma = IFNgamma - untreated,
                           levels = design)
fit <- lmFit(gse4hr, design)
fit <- eBayes(contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts))
```

We rank genes by the limma t-statistic. `fit$t` has one column per contrast,
with genes as row names:

```{r}
ranks <- list(IFNalpha = fit$t[, "IFNalpha"],
              IFNgamma = fit$t[, "IFNgamma"])
lengths(ranks)
```

## Making gene sets

`getGeneSets()` takes the `topK` genes with the largest weights in each
signature, which are the genes that go up after the perturbation. Use
`direction = "down"` for the genes that go down, or `direction = "both"`
for both (`_UP` and `_DN` sets). Passing the genes of the DE profile as
`universe` picks the top genes among those that fgsea can use, so every
gene set keeps `topK` genes. Both comparisons come from the same arrays, so
they share one gene universe.

```{r}
geneSets <- getGeneSets(signatures, topK = 100, universe = names(ranks$IFNalpha))
length(geneSets)
```

A positive NES means the DE profile goes the same way as the perturbation;
a negative NES means it goes the opposite way.

## Running fgsea

```{r}
set.seed(42)
fgseaRes <- lapply(ranks, function(stats) {
    fgsea(pathways = geneSets, stats = stats)
})
```

```{r}
plotTopSignatures <- function(fgseaRes, stats) {
    topUp <- fgseaRes[ES > 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
    topDown <- fgseaRes[ES < 0][head(order(pval), n = 10), pathway]
    plotGseaTable(geneSets[c(topUp, rev(topDown))], stats, fgseaRes, gseaParam = 0.5)
}
```

### IFN-alpha vs untreated

```{r}
head(fgseaRes$IFNalpha[order(pval)], 10)
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plotTopSignatures(fgseaRes$IFNalpha, ranks$IFNalpha)
```

```{r}
plotEnrichment(geneSets[["GENE_FAMILY_IFNA"]], ranks$IFNalpha) +
    labs(title = "GENE_FAMILY_IFNA", subtitle = "IFN-alpha vs untreated")
```

### IFN-gamma vs untreated

```{r}
head(fgseaRes$IFNgamma[order(pval)], 10)
```

```{r, fig.height = 6}
plotTopSignatures(fgseaRes$IFNgamma, ranks$IFNgamma)
```

```{r}
plotEnrichment(geneSets[["IFNG"]], ranks$IFNgamma) +
    labs(title = "IFNG", subtitle = "IFN-gamma vs untreated")
```

## Mouse signatures

Mouse signatures are loaded the same way. The top 50 genes of the
IFNG signature:

```{r}
mouseSignatures <- loadSignatures("mmu", geneId = "symbol")
dim(mouseSignatures)
getGeneSets(mouseSignatures, topK = 50)[["IFNG"]]
```
